Want to create and sell digital products? Here's what you actually do. 👇  1. Start with a problem. What problem are you solving for someone else? The best digital products make something easier, faster, or less overwhelming. 2. Create the solution. Turn what you know into something useful—a guide, checklist, planner, workbook, template, printable, mini-course, or resource. 3. Choose where to sell it. You can sell digital products through platforms like Etsy, Teachers Pay Teachers, Stan Store, or your own website. Choose the platform that makes sense for your product and audience. You can also publish them on Amazon Kindle Direct Publishing or Google Play.  4. Market it. Creating the product is only HALF the job. People have to find it! Use Pinterest, TikTok,  email, a blog, or search-friendly content to show people how your product solves their problem. 5. Learn from the first one...then create another. Your first product doesn't have to build financial freedom. It's your starting point. Create one useful product. Learn how to sell it. Improve. Then create another. Over time, you can build a collection of digital products that can be purchased while you're teaching, spending time with family, or simply living your life.  That's what I love about learning skills that can create income from home. I'm not looking for another job. I'm building more ways to earn—and more choices for my future. Financial freedom doesn't have to start with something huge. It can start with one product that solves one problem. Your audience isn’t going to buy your digital product simply because you keep telling them it’s in your link in the bio.. They need to understand why it’s relevant to them, what it could help them with and why they’d want it in the first place. Here are 5 things to bring into your content… 1. Talk about a problem your ideal buyer is struggling with like on a daily basis.  Show them you understand what’s frustrating them. Get specific about what they’re experiencing so they recognize themselves in your content. 2. Talk about what THEY WANT instead. What are they trying to achieve? What would life or business look like if they could overcome that problem? Give them something to connect with.  3. Connect their problem to your digital product. Help them see how what you sell relates to what they’re struggling with. Don’t leave them wondering how your product fits into the picture. 4. Explain why the features matter. Don’t stop at telling people what’s included. Explain what those things help them do and why it should matter to them. 5. Help them picture the life or the problem solved.  What does their life look like when their problem is solved?  Show them what moving from where they are now to where they want to be could look like with the help of your digital product. Remember….your content isn’t there to give people a tour of everything inside your product. It’s there to help the right person see why it matters to them and why it’s worth taking a closer look.
